findings.title: Production application deploys have no working manual-approval gate
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:565-571 — the prod deploy job attaches `environment: prod-approval`, with a comment stating the approval itself is a GitHub repository setting that cannot be enforced from the file

docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md:16-19 — `prod-approval` section: 'Required reviewers (1+) must be configured in GitHub ... none are configured yet, so the approval gate is not yet in force'
docs/RELEASING.md:96-105 — Approval gate section: until reviewers are added the prod job 'still runs ... without pausing and there is no working manual-approval gate'

.github/workflows/supabase-migrations.yml:28-34 — prod migrations run `supabase db push` under the `prod` environment, which also needs 1+ required reviewers per the matrix (CI-004), not under `prod-approval`
findings.impact: A merge-capable (or admin) account that lands a commit on `main` reaches production (deploy + prod DB migrations) with no second human gate. Branch protection is the only control, and migrations run under an environment whose protection rules are also unset.
findings.recommendation: Operator: configure 1+ required reviewers on `prod-approval` and `prod` in GitHub Settings -> Environments, then dispatch deploy-do deploy_target=prod and confirm it pauses at 'Waiting for approval'; alternatively migrate supabase-migrations to `prod-approval` after moving its environment-scoped values. Record the verification in docs/RELEASING.md.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: deploy-do.yml:571 still attaches prod-approval and both docs still state reviewers are not configured — code side is done, operator side unchanged. Residual added at this commit: prod migrations depend on reviewers on `prod` (supabase-migrations.yml:34), so both environments need the setting.

findings.title: Branch-protection-as-code has a likely-mismatched required check and permits admin bypass
evidence: .github/branch-protection/main.json:4-10 — contexts are the emitted check-run names: 'Test / test (20.x)', 'Lint / lint (20.x)', 'TypeCheck / typecheck', 'E2E / e2e (20.x)', 'Dependency Review / review'
.github/branch-protection/main.json:12-17 and develop.json:10-14 — `enforce_admins: true`, `require_code_owner_reviews: true`, `required_approving_review_count: 1`, `dismiss_stale_reviews: true`
.github/workflows/validate.yml:33-39 — every deploy gate runs `node scripts/check-required-checks.mjs`, which fails when a required context is not emitted by any workflow job
scripts/check-required-checks.mjs:29-37,101-118 — derives emitted check-run names from workflow name + job id + matrix value and compares them to the committed JSON

manual parity walk at 8d299b8d: test.yml (job `test`, matrix 20.x), lint.yml (job `lint`, matrix 20.x), typecheck.yml (job `typecheck`), e2e.yml (job `e2e`, matrix 20.x), dependency-review.yml (job `review`) all match the five contexts
findings.impact: The committed protection payload now resolves to real check-runs, so PRs are not stuck on 'Expected', and admins cannot bypass the checks once the JSON is applied. Residual risk is that the committed JSON is not automatically applied or drift-checked against live GitHub settings.
findings.recommendation: Keep the check-required-checks guard. Add a scheduled read-only drift check comparing live branch protection (gh api) to the committed JSON, and document the repo-admin apply step in docs/CI.md. (Live application itself is tracked by the branch-protection domain.)
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: static walk of all five contexts against workflow name/job/matrix matches; check-required-checks.mjs is wired into validate.yml:33-39. Node is not installed in the audit container, so the script itself was not executed — parity was re-derived by reading the parser and workflows. Live GitHub application remains a repo-admin action.

.github/workflows/test.yml:54-65 — the same composite runs on PRs against `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`
findings.impact: Resolved: a leaked credential introduced by a direct push to main is now diffed against the pushed commit's parent and fails the deploy gate.

findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: push path uses event.before + zero-SHA fallback; matches the fix merged as mainecybertech#75.

findings.title: Infrastructure changes are no longer gated in CI (terraform-do is manual-dispatch only)
evidence: .github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:3-21 — triggers are `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` only; `apply` input defaults false; header says push/PR triggers were removed pending token rotation and environment protection
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:14-15,36-38 — weekly plan-only schedule exists but the plan job is skipped unless `vars.TF_DRIFT_PLAN_ENABLED == 'true'`
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:99-110 — world-open SSH allowlist rejected; :176-196 validate/e2e/migration gates; :198-236 prod apply behind `prod-approval`
docs/CI.md:99-107 — documents the dormant weekly drift plan and the operator prerequisites (rotate DO_API_TOKEN, set TF_DRIFT_PLAN_ENABLED)
findings.impact: Infrastructure drift is not detected automatically by default and PRs cannot run plan on infra changes; re-enabling PR/push triggers is operator-gated on the DO token and environment protection. The apply path itself is gated and validated when run manually.
findings.recommendation: Operator: rotate DO_API_TOKEN, set TF_DRIFT_PLAN_ENABLED=true, then re-enable a PR/push plan trigger (plan-only; apply stays input-gated) so infra changes get a reviewable plan.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: manual+drift-only design is deliberate and documented; drift run remains dormant behind the repo variable. Residual is operator-gated, unchanged.

findings.title: Chromatic visual-regression job is permanently non-blocking

findings.impact: Visual regressions in packages/ui can never block a merge or deploy, and the failure is buried in a green pipeline. The docs disagree about whether this is intentional, so reviewers may trust a control that is not in force.
findings.recommendation: Fix the Storybook build (SB_BUILDER-WEBPACK5_0002), then remove continue-on-error and add Chromatic (or a Storybook build job) to the required checks; until then align AGENTS.md:635 with the config.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: continue-on-error: true still present (chromatic.yml:28); not re-checked previously (was carried open from run 20261002).

findings.title: Terraform apply is manual and drift detection is not automated
evidence: .github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:14-15 — weekly `schedule` for the drift plan

findings.impact: The drift-detection code is implemented but inactive by default: without the operator variable, scheduled runs do nothing and drift is not detected. This is the same operator prerequisite as the terraform gating finding.
findings.recommendation: Operator: rotate DO_API_TOKEN and set TF_DRIFT_PLAN_ENABLED=true (and provision ADMIN_IP_RANGES) so the weekly drift plan actually runs and alerts; then keep the schedule.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: drift plan + fail-on-drift step exist but are dormant behind TF_DRIFT_PLAN_ENABLED (terraform-do.yml:38). Status downgraded from the register's verified-fixed because the automated drift check does not run by default; enablement is operator-gated.

findings.title: Secret scanner misses the platform's own token formats and scans diffs only
evidence: .github/workflows/secret-history-scan.yml:5-12,27-47 — weekly/manual full-history gitleaks scan (v8.30.1 pinned + SHA-256 verified), `--redact --exit-code 1`, JSON report artifact
.github/workflows/secret-history-scan.yml:49-51 — scripts/ci/verify-gitleaks-config.sh proves the allowlist still catches a synthetic key
.gitleaks.toml:1-10 — default ruleset extended with value/line-scoped allowlists only
.github/actions/secret-scan/action.yml:14 — the PR/push diff scanner still uses the fixed provider list (AKIA/ghp_/sk_/xox/JWT/PEM); no platform-specific token formats
findings.impact: Half resolved: full history is now scanned weekly with a pinned gitleaks, but the per-PR/push scanner is still a fixed provider list and the history scan is not per-commit, so a platform-specific token introduced and removed between weekly runs would be caught only by the diff scanner (if the format is in its list).
findings.recommendation: Extend the diff scanner patterns (or run gitleaks on the diff with the default ruleset) and document the coverage in docs/CI.md.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: gitleaks full-history scan + scoped allowlist added since the carry-forward; diff-scanner format gap remains.

findings.title: Unused permission grants across deploy/test workflows
evidence: .github/workflows/test.yml:16-18 — `security-events: write` but no step uploads SARIF to code scanning; the Trivy SARIF is only uploaded as an artifact (.github/actions/dependency-audit/action.yml:44-65)

.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:23-26 — `pull-requests: write` while the only PR-comment step (:138-152) is guarded by `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` and the workflow no longer has a pull_request trigger (:3-21)
findings.impact: Two write scopes no step can consume remain on every run, increasing token blast radius if a step or third-party action is compromised.
findings.recommendation: Drop `security-events: write` from test.yml (or actually upload the SARIF to code scanning) and drop `pull-requests: write` from terraform-do.yml (or delete the unreachable step).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: both grants still present (was carried open from run 20261002).

findings.title: DB restore test uses an unpinned `postgres:16-alpine` image
evidence: .github/workflows/db-restore-test.yml:110-117 — `docker run ... postgres:16-alpine` (tag only, no digest)
.github/dependabot.yml:51-92 — Dependabot docker entries cover apps/api, apps/web, apps/worker and infra/digitalocean, but not this throwaway CI image
findings.impact: The restore test's database binary can change under the workflow between runs (tag drift), so a future failure may not reproduce and a compromised/updated tag is not review-gated.
findings.recommendation: Pin the image by digest (and add a Dependabot docker entry or a scheduled digest-refresh comment) or install a pinned postgres package.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: still tag-pinned only (was carried open from run 20261002).

findings.title: No release/tagging workflow and no post-merge release artifact
evidence: .github/workflows/ contains 20 workflows and none is a release/tag workflow (ls .github/workflows)
docs/RELEASING.md:47-53 — 'There is no git tag requirement — the commit SHA is authoritative'; releases are GHCR images tagged with the deploy SHA
REL-P1-001 (follow-up register) — partially-fixed: SBOM binds the commit but no annotated tags / release workflow exist
findings.impact: There is no repository artifact that marks a production release, so release notes, rollback targets and audit evidence rely on remembering the deploy SHA; GitHub Releases/tags are absent.
findings.recommendation: Add a small release workflow (on prod promotion: create an annotated tag from VERSION+date, attach the SBOM and a release-notes body from templates/RELEASE_NOTES_TEMPLATE.md) or record the owner decision to stay SHA-only.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: no release/tag workflow; RELEASING.md still documents SHA-as-release (was carried open from run 20261002).

findings.title: e2e is required on `main` but the documented flakiness makes it an unstable hard gate
evidence: .github/branch-protection/main.json:8 — 'E2E / e2e (20.x)' is a required check on main
AGENTS.md:93 — 'E2E has known run-to-run flakiness: data-dependent tests ... fail intermittently due to CI API/Supabase contention'
docs/RELEASING.md:148-150 — 'E2E has known run-to-run flakiness ... re-run before treating a failure as a product regression'
.github/workflows/e2e.yml:75-88,163-169 — local Supabase + seeded data dependency; retries around infra steps only
findings.impact: A required gate that is known to fail spuriously trains reviewers to re-run rather than investigate, and can block merges to main for non-product reasons. The path-filter problem (separate finding) compounds it.
findings.recommendation: Quarantine or retry the flaky specs, then keep E2E required; document the triage path in docs/CI.md.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: E2E still required on main and the flakiness note is still in AGENTS.md/RELEASING.md (was carried open from run 20261002).

findings.title: Missing per-job timeouts and minor workflow hygiene gaps
evidence: 9 workflows have zero `timeout-minutes` anywhere: a11y-breadth.yml, backup-dispatch.yml, chromatic.yml, db-backup.yml, dependency-review.yml, lint.yml, supabase-migrations.yml, terraform-do.yml, typecheck.yml (grep -c)
.github/workflows/validate.yml:10-11,72-73,83-84,94-95 — audit/lint/typecheck/prompt-provenance jobs have no timeout (test and secrets-scan do)
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:35-43,198-236 — plan/apply jobs have no timeout (a hung terraform apply holds the concurrency lock indefinitely)
findings.impact: A hung job (network stall, interactive prompt, stuck registry pull) can occupy a runner and, for terraform/migrations, hold the per-branch concurrency lock, delaying every later run on that ref.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit timeout-minutes to every job (5-15 for lint/typecheck/audit, 30-60 for terraform/migrations); keep command_timeout on the SSH steps as the inner bound.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: timeout coverage unchanged (was carried open from run 20261002).

findings.title: E2E is a required check on main but path-filtered, so PRs that miss its paths can never satisfy branch protection
evidence: .github/branch-protection/main.json:4-10 — 'E2E / e2e (20.x)' is a required context on main

.github/workflows/e2e.yml:12-22 — pull_request `paths:` limited to apps/web/e2e/**, apps/web/playwright.config.ts, apps/web/app/**, apps/web/components/**, packages/**, supabase/seeds/**, supabase/migrations/**, .github/workflows/e2e.yml

.github/workflows/test.yml:10-12 — comment records the exact BP-P2-004 class: 'a path-filtered workflow never reports on docs-only PRs — leaving them blocked or unguarded'; test/lint/typecheck were fixed this way, e2e was not
a PR touching only docs/**, scripts/**, infra/**, apps/api/** or any other workflow file triggers no E2E run, so the required check stays 'Expected — Waiting for status to be reported'
findings.impact: Docs-only or API-only PRs to main cannot merge without touching an E2E-matched path (or an admin bypass, which branch protection now forbids). This is a merge-blocking drift class the check-required-checks guard does not detect because the check-run name matches.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `paths:` filter from e2e.yml's pull_request trigger (keep it for push/workflow_call if desired), or make E2E non-required on main and rely on the deploy gate, or add a companion 'e2e skipped' job that reports success on non-matching PRs. Extend scripts/check-required-checks.mjs (or a new check) to flag path-filtered required workflows.
findings.note: new at 8d299b8d: found by enumerating required contexts against workflow triggers (extended verification check). This is the concrete residual of BP-P2-004 (branch-protection domain row) for e2e.yml specifically. Config evidence is high; whether live branch protection exactly matches the committed JSON is unverifiable from the repo (repo-admin action).

findings.title: Backup dispatcher duplicates the backup workflows now that they exist on the default branch
evidence: .github/workflows/backup-dispatch.yml:21-25 — schedules at 04:00 daily, 05:00 daily, Mon 06:00; :85-93 dispatches db-backup.yml / db-restore-test.yml / storage-backup.yml with `--ref develop`
.github/workflows/db-backup.yml:3-4, storage-backup.yml:19-20, db-restore-test.yml:3-4 — the same schedules exist in the workflows themselves, and all three files are present on main at 8d299b8d
.github/workflows/backup-dispatch.yml:3-9 — header says it exists because those workflows were added on develop and 'never ran' from main; the DR-P0-001 fix (PR #93) promoted them to main
.github/workflows/backup-dispatch.yml:60-67 — the job fails loudly when SCHEDULE_DISPATCH_TOKEN is unset, so an unprovisioned token produces a daily red run while the real backup can still succeed
findings.impact: The default branch now runs each scheduled backup/mirror/restore test twice (once natively on main, once dispatched onto develop): duplicate dumps/mirrors, duplicate runner and DB load, and two independent failure signals for one DR path. The two copies can also drift apart in later PRs.
findings.recommendation: Keep one trigger source: either delete backup-dispatch.yml now that the workflows are on main, or remove the schedule blocks from the three workflows if dispatching to develop is preferred. Record the choice in docs/CI.md; if the dispatcher stays, gate it so it does not double-run.
findings.note: new at 8d299b8d: consequence of promoting develop to main (DR-P0-001 fix) without retiring the dispatcher. Config-level evidence is high; live Actions run history is not visible from the repo, hence medium confidence on the duplicate runs actually occurring.

findings.title: Workflow documentation drift: docs list a removed workflow, omit a live one, and misstate gate behavior
evidence: README.md:326, AGENTS.md:300, review.md:306 and docs/CI.md:28 document `wireguard-endpoint.yml`, which does not exist (removed in 52304944; 20 files in .github/workflows)
docs/CI.md workflow table omits .github/workflows/secret-history-scan.yml (live weekly gitleaks full-history scan)
docs/CI.md:117 says A11y breadth is `continue-on-error: true`, but a11y-breadth.yml:18-22 has no continue-on-error (it calls e2e.yml)

## Executive Summary

The CI/CD estate at `8d299b8d` is well above the baseline for a repo of this size: 20 workflows, every external action pinned to a commit SHA, least-privilege `permissions` on every workflow, per-ref concurrency groups (deploys never cancelled mid-flight), composite actions shared between the PR gate and the deploy gate, provenance/SBOM attestations verified fail-closed before deploy, a pre-push migration dry-run plan uploaded as an artifact, and a restore test that asserts integrity floors rather than printing numbers. The branch-protection payload was corrected and is guarded by `check-required-checks.mjs`, which closes the previous P1 class.

The remaining risks are mostly *operator-gated settings* and *drift classes the guards do not cover*:

1. **The prod approval gate is still not in force** (CI-P1-001): the workflow attaches `prod-approval`, but the docs themselves state no reviewers are configured; prod migrations additionally depend on reviewers on `prod`. Combined with the unprovisioned prod secrets (CI-P1-003), production is effectively not deployable by design — safe, but not releasable.
2. **E2E is required on `main` but path-filtered** (new, P2): a docs-only or API-only PR can never satisfy the required check. test/lint/typecheck were fixed for exactly this (BP-P2-004); e2e was missed.
3. **The backup dispatcher now duplicates schedules** (new, P2): the DR-P0-001 fix promoted the backup workflows to main, but `backup-dispatch.yml` still dispatches copies onto develop.
4. **Two smaller verification rows changed state on re-check**: the terraform drift plan is dormant behind `TF_DRIFT_PLAN_ENABLED` (partially-fixed, not fixed), and the actionlint lint fixes are incomplete with no workflow-lint gate (partially-fixed).

Recommended next actions: configure `prod-approval`/`prod` reviewers and prod secrets (operator); remove the e2e `paths:` filter on `pull_request`; retire the backup dispatcher; enable the terraform drift variable after token rotation; and wire a real workflow-lint job.

## Detailed Review

### Item: Required-check gate map (what each check executes)

- Evidence: `.github/branch-protection/main.json:4-10`, `develop.json:4-8`; `test.yml:26-65`; `lint.yml:21-37`; `typecheck.yml:21-32`; `e2e.yml:39-182`; `dependency-review.yml:10-30`; `.github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:21-63`.
- What it does: `Test / test (20.x)` runs the coverage suite plus OpenAPI validation/audit, docs counts/links, DB-type freshness, RLS hygiene, membership-predicate lint and review.md mirror, plus audit/license/Trivy/secrets jobs. `Lint` and `TypeCheck` run the workspace commands. `E2E / e2e (20.x)` boots local Supabase + API + web and runs Playwright/axe. `Dependency Review / review` blocks high-severity and denied licenses on the PR diff.
- Drift classes the required checks do **not** cover: path-filtered workflows that never report (E2E — new finding); committed-vs-live branch protection drift (BP-P2-003, owned by the branch-protection domain); workflow YAML/shell lint (no actionlint job); docs-vs-tree drift (new finding).
- Bypass analysis: `enforce_admins: true`, `allow_force_pushes: false`, `allow_deletions: false`, `required_conversation_resolution: true` in both JSONs. There is no `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run` anywhere, and `[skip ci]` on a PR leaves required checks pending (blocks, not bypasses). The remaining bypass vector is repo-admin mutation of the protection payload itself, which has no in-repo audit (BP-P2-002/003 domain).

### Item: Deploy flow (deployment flow)

- Evidence: `deploy-do.yml:16-43` (push to main/develop + dispatch), `:101-182` (resolve-ip from DO API → TF state → var), `:184-380` (3 builds + Trivy image scan + digest-bound SBOM + provenance attestation), `:391-515` (`verify-attestations` fail-closed incl. reviewed legacy rollback allow-list), `:517-535` (validate always; e2e+migrate prod-only), `:537-571` (fail-closed `needs` expression, `prod-approval`), `:575-935` (SSH deploy, `.env` via printf, health gate, auto-rollback, host-key-pinned health check).
- Deployment flow: push/merge to `main` (or dispatch `deploy_target=prod`) → setup → resolve-ip (`prod` env) → build×3 ∥ validate → e2e+migrate (prod only) → verify attestations → deploy (`prod-approval`, health-gated, auto-rollback). Dev (`develop`) skips e2e/migrate and uses the `dev` environment.
- Missing controls: the approval pause itself depends on GitHub environment settings (CI-P1-001); prod secrets are unprovisioned (CI-P1-003).

### Item: Migration flow

- Evidence: `supabase-migrations.yml:21-25` (serialized per ref), `:30-34` (`prod` env on main), `:57-60` (CLI pinned 2.107.0), `:67-83` (pre-push `db push --dry-run` teed + artifact before the real push), `:90-127` (post-push `db diff` gate, ANSI-stripped, `allow_drift=1` only on reviewed dispatch).
- Assessment: this is a strong flow (IR-P2-006/IR-P1-002/DATA-P2-004 fixes verified). Residual: approval depends on reviewers configured on the `prod` environment, which the matrix says are not set.

### Item: Secrets handling

- Evidence: `secret-scan/action.yml:14` (provider pattern list), `:15-27` (event.before on push, base.sha on PR), `:43-62` (tracked local-secret-file guard); `secret-history-scan.yml:27-51` (gitleaks 8.30.1 pinned + SHA-256 verified, full history, redacted, allowlist negative test); `.gitleaks.toml` (scoped allowlists only); `secret-rotation-reminder.yml` (quarterly issue); deploy secrets forwarded via `envs:`/`printf` and never interpolated into remote shell text (`deploy-do.yml:644-716`).
- Residual: diff-scanner formats are a fixed provider list; full-history scan is weekly, not per-commit.

### Item: Permissions, OIDC, concurrency, caching, artifacts

- Permissions: least-privilege at workflow level; `verify-attestations` re-scopes to read (`deploy-do.yml:399-406`). Unused `security-events: write` (test.yml:18) and `pull-requests: write` (terraform-do.yml:26) remain.
- OIDC: `id-token: write` only for attestations (`deploy-do.yml:34`, `build-push.yml:15`); no cloud OIDC trust (DO/CF still token-based).
- Concurrency: per-ref groups everywhere it matters; deploys (`cancel-in-progress: false`) and migrations/terraform are serialized; PR runs cancel superseded (`test/lint/typecheck/e2e/sbom/chromatic/codeql`).
- Caching: pnpm store keyed on lockfile (`setup-pnpm/action.yml:38-47`), Playwright browser cache (`e2e.yml:55-62`), buildx `type=gha` caches.
- Artifacts: dry-run plan before push, Trivy SARIF (7d), SBOMs (30d), Playwright reports on failure (7d), tfplan (1d); retention set on all.

- Evidence: `main.json`/`develop.json` (above); `check-required-checks.mjs` wired into `validate.yml:33-39`; `CODEOWNERS:1-44`; `dependabot.yml:1-102` (npm/github-actions/docker×5/terraform, weekly, target develop).

### NEW — E2E is a required check on main but path-filtered, so PRs that miss its paths can never satisfy branch protection

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: medium · Status: open · Owner: platform/CI owner · Target: this month
- Evidence: `main.json:8` requires `E2E / e2e (20.x)`; `e2e.yml:12-22` path-filters `pull_request`; `test.yml:10-12` records the same class (BP-P2-004) fixed for test/lint/typecheck only — this is the concrete residual for e2e.yml (BP-P2-004 is also tracked by the branch-protection domain).
- Why it matters: docs-only or API-only PRs to main stay blocked on a check that will never report.
- Recommended fix: drop the `paths:` filter on `pull_request` (or make E2E non-required / add a reporting companion job); extend the required-check guard to flag path-filtered required workflows.

### NEW — Backup dispatcher duplicates the backup workflows now that they exist on the default branch

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: medium · Status: open · Owner: platform/CI owner · Target: this month
- Evidence: `backup-dispatch.yml:21-25,85-93` schedules + dispatches `--ref develop`; `db-backup.yml:3-4`, `storage-backup.yml:19-20`, `db-restore-test.yml:3-4` have the same schedules and are all on main; the dispatcher header (`:3-9`) explains it predates the promotion (DR-P0-001, PR #93).
- Why it matters: each DR job now runs twice (main + dispatched develop), duplicating dumps/mirrors/restore tests; an unset `SCHEDULE_DISPATCH_TOKEN` produces daily red runs while the real backup may succeed.
- Recommended fix: keep one trigger source — delete the dispatcher or the three schedule blocks; document the choice.
